sections.h2: Where is Rexburg, Idaho, and how is the city laid out?
sections.html:
Rexburg is the county seat and largest city of Madison County in eastern Idaho. It also anchors the Rexburg micropolitan area, which takes in Madison and Fremont counties.

The city covers about 10 square miles at an elevation of 4,862 feet. Much of it, including the campus of Brigham Young University-Idaho and the Rexburg Idaho Temple, sits on top of an old shield volcano. Lava fields lie to the west and south, and the volcanic soil is the reason the surrounding country is known for potatoes.

Almost every Rexburg address is inside the Madison School District 321 boundary. The Wikipedia entry on the city notes that a few blocks belong to the Sugar-Salem Joint School District 322 instead, so a seller near that edge should confirm the district before listing the house or describing it to a buyer.

sections.h2: What is Rexburg's history, and does the Teton Dam flood still matter?
sections.html:
Rexburg was incorporated in 1883 and takes its name from founder Thomas Edwin Ricks. The population was 1,081 in 1900 and 39,409 in 2020.

The biggest single event in local memory is the Teton Dam failure in June 1976. The Teton River runs through northern Rexburg, and the flood left most of the city underwater for several days. The Teton Dam Flood museum in the basement of the Rexburg Tabernacle covers that history.

Buyers and lenders ask whether a parcel is in a mapped flood area, so ask your title company or insurer for the flood status of your address. If the house has had water in the basement, say so up front.

sections.h2: How does Rexburg's climate affect an older house?
sections.html:
Rexburg has long, cold winters and short, dry summers. The 1991 to 2020 normals at BYU-Idaho put the average daily high in January at 29.5 degrees Fahrenheit and the average low at 14.2. The record low is minus 36, and frosts have been recorded in every month of the year.

Snow matters more than rain. The station averages 54.9 inches of snow a year against 12.63 inches of total precipitation, and the heaviest single month on record was 43.5 inches in December 1983. The deepest snow cover, 38 inches, has happened twice, in March 1985 and February 2008.

That pattern puts stress on a few parts of a house:

  • Roofs: long snow cover and repeated freeze and thaw wear shingles, flashing and gutters.
  • Heating: a furnace that fails in January is an urgent repair, and buyers know it.
  • Plumbing: pipes in crawl spaces and exterior walls are the usual freeze risk.

An old roof or furnace tends to show up in a buyer's inspection, which leads to repair requests. Selling as-is moves that risk to the buyer.

sections.h2: What does the student rental market mean for people selling a house in Rexburg?
sections.html:
Rexburg's median age was 22.8 in 2020, and BYU-Idaho is the reason. Houses near campus are often rented, so some owners here are landlords instead of residents.

That creates a few common situations for sellers:

  • An investor owns a house with students on a lease that ends in April or August, and wants to sell without disrupting the tenants.
  • A family inherits a house that has been rented for years, with deferred maintenance.

A house with tenants in place can be sold with the lease attached. Read the lease and any deposit obligations before you sign a sale contract.

sections.h2: What are Rexburg's short-term rental rules?
sections.html:
Rexburg requires a short-term rental to be registered with the city, inspected for life safety and renewed every year. The rules come from city Ordinance 1308 and the Building department's short-term rental page.

If you own a house that has been used as a nightly rental, or if your buyer plans to run it as one, these requirements are worth knowing:

  • Zoning decides the occupancy rule. In the TAG, RR1, RR2, LDR1, LDR2 and LDR3 zones the owner or a manager must live on-site. In MDR1, MDR2, HDR1 and HDR2 the owner, a manager or the owner's agent must be available in Madison County.
  • Parking must cover two spaces for the house plus one more for each rented room.
  • A life safety inspection is required, and the city lists egress window sizes, smoke and carbon monoxide detectors and a kitchen fire extinguisher among the items checked.
  • Three violations of city ordinances at the property can lead to revocation of the registration.

Ask the city whether an existing registration can transfer to a new owner before you promise that to a buyer.

sections.h2: When are Madison County property taxes due, and what happens at closing?
sections.html:
Madison County property tax is due in two halves: the first half by December 20 and the second half by June 20 of the next year. The Treasurer's Office is at 134 E Main in Rexburg, and the phone is 208-359-6200, option 5.

DateWhat happens
April 15Last day to file for the Homeowners Exemption and Circuit Breaker in the Assessor's Office
June 20Second half of taxes due
Fourth Monday of JuneLast day to file a protest of value with the Assessor
December 20At least the first half of the current year's taxes due

If the first half is not paid by December 20, the county adds a 2 percent late charge on December 21, and interest runs at 1 percent per month starting January 1. For the second half, the 2 percent charge applies on June 21, but interest counts from January 1, not June 21.

The notice covers the calendar year. A seller who closes in the middle of the year usually settles the current tax with the buyer through the title company. The county adds that not receiving a bill does not excuse the tax.

If taxes on real property go unpaid for three years, the county can deed the property to itself under Idaho Code 63-1002, after notice by certified mail to recorded interest holders and four weeks of newspaper publication. The owner can redeem before the sale by paying all delinquent years plus the current year, under Idaho Code 63-1007. For an owner behind on taxes, a sale that pays the county at closing can end that clock.

sections.h2: Which schools, hospital and services serve Rexburg homes?
sections.html:
Madison School District 321 serves nearly all of Rexburg. Its six elementary schools are Adams, Burton, Hibbard, Kennedy, Lincoln and South Fork.

Madison Memorial Hospital is just east of downtown. BYU-Idaho, the largest institution in town, is private and owned by the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale work for a house in Rexburg?
sections.html:
A cash sale in Rexburg follows the same Idaho closing steps as any other sale, minus the buyer's mortgage. You tell the buyer about the house, receive a written offer, and decide whether to accept. A title company handles the deed, the payoff of any liens and the settlement of property tax.

Cash Home Buyers purchases houses as-is, with no fees, commissions or closing costs to you, and you owe nothing if you turn the offer down.

Before you decide between routes, compare them on the points that usually matter to Rexburg sellers:

  • Timeline: a traditional listing depends on showings and a buyer's financing, while a cash sale depends on the title work and the date you choose.
  • Condition: a listing invites inspection requests for roof, furnace and plumbing, and an as-is sale does not.
  • Costs: a listing normally involves an agent's commission and seller closing costs, so ask for a written estimate of both before you compare net proceeds.

sections.h2: What do sellers in Rexburg usually run into?
sections.html:
Sellers here usually face one of a few situations, each with a practical first step.

  • Inherited house: confirm who has authority to sign, gather the death certificate and any court papers, and check for unpaid taxes.
  • Behind on taxes or payments: get a written payoff figure from the lender and a balance from the Treasurer's Office.
  • Rental that needs work: list the repairs, read the lease and decide whether to sell with tenants.

If you are weighing options, you can also read our Idaho guides on property tax appeals, the homestead exemption and estate and inheritance tax, which are linked on this page. This article is general information about Rexburg and is not legal or tax advice. Confirm details with the county or a licensed professional.

faqs.q: What is the deadline for property tax in Rexburg?
faqs.a: Madison County property tax is due in two halves, by December 20 for the first half and June 20 for the second. A 2 percent late charge and 1 percent monthly interest apply after the deadline.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Rexburg house that has student tenants?
faqs.a: Yes. A house can be sold with a lease in place, and the buyer takes over the lease terms. Read the lease and any deposit obligations before you sign a sale contract.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to run a short-term rental in Rexburg?
faqs.a: Yes. The city requires registration, a life safety inspection and an annual renewal, and some zones require the owner or manager to live on-site. Three ordinance violations at a property can lead to revocation.

faqs.q: How much snow does Rexburg get, and does it hurt resale?
faqs.a: Rexburg averages 54.9 inches of snow a year. An old roof or furnace tends to show up in a buyer's inspection, which is one reason some owners sell as-is.

faqs.q: What if I owe back taxes on a Rexburg house?
faqs.a: Pay the oldest delinquency first, since the county applies payments that way. Real property unpaid for three years can be deeded to the county, but the owner can redeem before the sale by paying all delinquent years plus the current year.

faqs.q: Does Cash Home Buyers charge fees on a Rexburg sale?
faqs.a: No. We buy as-is with no fees, commissions or closing costs to you, and you owe nothing if you decline the offer.
